verdict.rationale: Grafana documents its own provisioning and observability-as-code system: dashboards, data sources and other configuration are defined as files that can be version controlled and deployed through CI/CD pipelines. That covers the versioning part of the story. Review and rollback are only implied, through external Git workflows rather than any documented Grafana capability, and the evidence never says alert rules or other automations are included. missing for 10: documented review/approval workflow, documented rollback mechanism, explicit coverage of alert rules and other automations as code, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: You can define data sources and dashboards using files that can be version controlled, making GitOps more natural.
This approach lets you define dashboards, data sources, and other configurations in code, enabling version control, automated testing, and reliable deployments through CI/CD pipelines.
You can authenticate, manage multiple environments, and perform administrative tasks from the terminal. It’s suitable for CI/CD pipelines, local development
